about: The habit tracker plugin: a checklist of daily habits shown on the diary's day page, below the entry composer. These strings are fetched only when the user enables the plugin, and are merged into the app's main bundle under the `plugins.habits.` prefix — so a key written here as "title" is referenced in code as plugins.habits.title. Keys not listed under `keys` below still need translating; the notes exist for the ones whose meaning is not obvious from the English.

habits.where: A card on the diary’s day page below the composer, where habits are recorded but never created; the plugin’s own page at /plugins/habits, where they are created, retired and reviewed as a three-week grid; its name, description and reminder settings in the Plugins list in Settings; and, once its name appears as a tab, the Calendar page's own month grid, shaded by how many of that day's habits were met. The day card also carries a padlock on any day but today — every day except the one being lived opens read-only, and the padlock is what lets someone deliberately go back and correct one.

keys.name: The plugin's name in the Plugins list in Settings. A noun, not a sentence; the word a user would use for the feature.
keys.description: One line under the name in the Plugins list, explaining what enabling it does.
keys.title: Heading of the card on the day page. Usually identical to `name` — kept separate so a language that wants a longer heading than a list label can have one.
keys.empty: Shown when no habit has been created yet, on both the day card and the plugin page. Matter-of-fact, not encouraging: the user has not failed at anything.
keys.nameLabel: Accessible label for the add form's text field. Never displayed; read aloud by screen readers.
keys.namePlaceholder: Greyed-out example inside the add field. Should be a plausible small daily habit, localised to something ordinary in that language's culture rather than translated literally.
keys.streak: Read aloud beside a flame icon for a habit done two or more days running; the digit itself is shown visually. Plain and factual — the app never congratulates. Note the visual form is just the number, so this string is for screen readers and needs to stand alone as a sentence fragment.
keys.remove: Accessible label for the × button that deletes a habit. Never displayed.
keys.lastDays: Accessible name for the row of squares showing recent days. Never displayed.
keys.done: Read aloud for a filled square, after the date. A past-tense fragment, not a sentence.
keys.notDone: Read aloud for an empty square, after the date. Neutral — a blank day is not a failure.
keys.remindersTitle: Heading of the plugin’s own settings card, below the Plugins list. Native app only.
keys.remindersDescription: Under that heading. Says plainly that these are per-device, unlike the switch that enables the plugin — the one asymmetry in how plugin settings work.
keys.reminder: Switch label for the daily habit nudge.
keys.reminderDescription: Under the switch: what the notification is for.
keys.reminderTime: Label beside the time picker for the nudge.
keys.reminderTitle: Title of the Android notification. Just the feature name — the body carries the content.
keys.reminderBody: Body of that notification, when some of the day’s habits are still unticked. States the number left, nothing more: no encouragement, no guilt. It never fires when everything is done, so it is never a congratulation.
keys.dateColumn: Header of the first column in the Markdown export table. One word.
keys.emptyPageDescription: Second line of the plugin page’s empty state. Says what a habit can be, since the two kinds are the thing worth knowing before creating one.
keys.setUp: Button on the day card taking the user to the plugin page, where habits are created. Habits cannot be created from the day page.
keys.turnOff: Button on the day card, and the confirm button in its dialog, for switching the whole plugin off.
keys.turnOffDescription: Body of it. The reassurance is the point — nothing is deleted, and the switch is reversible — because turning a plugin off syncs to every device.
keys.allRetired: Shown on the day card when habits exist but every one of them is retired and none was recorded on this day.
keys.newHabit: Button on the plugin page that opens the creation form.
keys.doneOf: Progress counter in the day card’s header, e.g. 2/5. Digits and a slash in every language. Reused verbatim in the calendar page's tooltip for a day, once its "Habits" tab is picked — same numbers, same meaning, so it has to keep reading correctly there too, without the visible "Habits" heading beside it that the day card has.
keys.typeLabel: Label above the kind selector in the creation form.
keys.unitLabel: Optional label for what a count is measured in.
keys.unitPlaceholder: Example unit. Very short — it is shown beside the number on the day card.
keys.targetLabel: Optional daily goal for a count habit; the progress bar fills toward it.
keys.recordedDays: How many days this habit was ever recorded on, on its card. Also what decides whether it can be deleted or only retired.
keys.retire: Stops asking about a habit without deleting it. Used instead of delete once a habit has any recorded day, because those days are diary history. Avoid words that imply removal.
keys.restore: Brings a retired habit back into the day list.
keys.retiredCount: Label on the disclosure hiding retired habits on the plugin page.
keys.retiredOnDay: Label on the same disclosure on the day card, where it holds retired habits that *were* recorded on that particular day.
keys.hideRetired: The same disclosure’s label once open.
keys.markDone: The only *visible* label on a habit control: the button that records a yes/no habit for the day. It is a toggle, and the same word is shown whether or not the habit is done — the button's fill carries the state, so the word must read naturally both as what you are about to do and as what you have done. Very short; it sits at the end of a row that already holds the habit's name, and on a phone it shares that row with it. Not a congratulation.
keys.increase: Accessible label for the + button on a counted habit. Never displayed.
keys.decrease: Accessible label for the − button. Never displayed.
keys.typeBinary: One of five kinds in the creation selector: something that either happened or didn’t.
keys.typeTime: Kind: something measured in minutes and hours, with a stopwatch.
keys.typeScale: Kind: something judged on a sliding scale rather than counted.
keys.typeMood: Kind: five faces. Keep it to the everyday word for how you feel, not a clinical one.
keys.typeBinaryHint: One line under the selector explaining that kind. The five hints are what actually distinguish “a number” from “a rating” for someone meeting them for the first time.
keys.typeNumericHint: As above. Examples should be ordinary in that language’s culture rather than translated literally.
keys.typeTimeHint: As above. Mentions the stopwatch, which is the whole difference from a plain number.
keys.targetMinutesLabel: Goal field for a timed habit. Says “minutes” because the value is entered in minutes even though it is stored in seconds.
keys.targetMinutesPlaceholder: Example goal in minutes. A plain number.
keys.minLabel: Bottom of a rating scale, in the creation form. One word.
keys.maxLabel: Top of a rating scale. One word.
keys.start: Accessible label for the stopwatch play button. Never displayed.
keys.pause: Accessible label for the same button while running. Never displayed.
keys.clear: Accessible label for the × that resets a habit to “not recorded” for that day. Never displayed.
keys.cleared: Toast after clearing, alongside an Undo. Neutral — clearing is a correction, not a failure.
keys.mood1: Worst of the five faces. One word, everyday register; these read left to right as a scale.
keys.mood3: Middle of five — neutral, not negative.
keys.summaryBinary: One-line description under a habit’s name on its card, per kind.
keys.summaryNumeric: As above; `_target` is the variant when a daily goal is set.
keys.summaryTime: As above. {{target}} arrives already formatted, e.g. “30m”.
keys.editHabit: Title of the creation dialog when it is opened on an existing habit.
keys.typeFixed: Replaces the kind hint while editing, explaining why the selector is disabled.
keys.changeCount: Label on the disclosure holding a habit’s edit history.
keys.changeName: One line of that history. Use the quotation marks your language uses.
keys.changeGoal: One line: the daily goal before and after. {{from}} may be the word for “none”.
keys.changeUnit: One line: the unit before and after. An em dash stands for “no unit”.
keys.changeScale: One line: a rating’s bounds before and after, already formatted as “1–5”.
keys.noGoal: Stands in for a goal that was not set, inside changeGoal. Lower case — it sits mid-sentence.
keys.changesHeading: Heading of the edit-history section in the Markdown export, under the habit table.
keys.notSet: Announced by a rating slider that has no value yet. Visually this is an em dash; the string is what distinguishes “not answered” from “rated lowest” for a screen reader.
keys.edit: Accessible label for the value itself, which is a button that turns into a text field when pressed. Never displayed — the number is what is shown.
keys.unlock: Accessible name (and, on a pointer device, tooltip trigger) for the padlock button on any day but today, while it is locked. An action, not a description — "Unlock this day", not "Locked".
keys.lock: The same button's accessible name once tapped unlocked, offering to lock it again. "Lock this day", the mirror of `unlock`.
keys.dayLockedPast: Tooltip shown while the padlock is locked and the day being viewed is before today. Explains *why* editing is blocked and what tapping the button does, since the icon alone only shows the state, not the reason. Read on hover on the web; on the native app there is no tooltip, so `unlock`'s accessible name is what a screen reader gets instead — this string only needs to work as an on-hover explanation.
keys.dayLockedFuture: As above, for a day after today. A different reason (it hasn't happened yet, not that it's history), so a different sentence rather than one that tries to cover both.
keys.dayUnlockedHint: Tooltip once the day has been unlocked, on either side of today — the reason it was locked stops being the point once you can edit it, so this doesn't distinguish past from future.

tone: Same as the main app: plain, calm, second person, no exclamation marks. This is a private diary, not a productivity coach — never congratulate, never nag, and never use streak language that frames a missed day as failure.

languageNotes.en: Reference language; source strings are authored here.
languageNotes.es: Tú, not usted, matching the rest of the app.
languageNotes.it: Tu, not Lei, matching the rest of the app.
languageNotes.ja: です・ます, matching the rest of the app. Only the unsuffixed `streak` key is needed — Japanese has a single plural category.
languageNotes.zh: Simplified Chinese, matching the rest of the app. Only the unsuffixed `streak` key is needed — Chinese has a single plural category.
